scope: local offline bundle syntax review; no runtime admission or complete dependency isolation claim

syntaxReview.scope: Syntax inspection only; does not exclude aliases, generated code, builtin capabilities or arbitrary loader mechanisms

checks: The generated artifact is parsed as JavaScript with the existing pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 parser; syntax errors, invalid UTF-8 and bytes outside the nonempty 4 MiB bound refuse.
Seven dynamic import forms refuse without evaluating fixture code: literal builtin, variable, template, nested URL, unreachable branch, commented data URL and import options.
Three external static import/re-export forms refuse. Builtin declarations pass; inert import-like strings, comments and regular expressions do not trigger refusal.

The actual artifact has zero import expressions, builtin-only static module specifiers and unchanged output bytes. Parser implementation bytes are fingerprinted before loading and rechecked after inspection.
Existing executable override refusal, exclusive output handling, CommonJS guard and 23 standalone adapter fixtures continue to pass.

limitations: This is syntactic inspection, not proof that arbitrary package resolution or code execution is impossible. Aliases, generated code, alternate loaders and builtin capabilities require separate review.
The existing CommonJS guard remains a separate control. Builtin modules can access files, processes and networks; no network sandbox is claimed.
The parser is selected from the existing dependency graph and its observed module hash is recorded. This does not attest its origin or continuously bind execution to file bytes.
Successful local artifact fixtures do not admit a Linux rehearsal host, replace actual fresh genesis compilation, establish backing or authorize deployment.
All previous artifacts, failed attempts, runtime identity and canonical ledger remain unchanged.
